issues.description: Unsupported statement: "Yamoah et al. achieved 88% sensitivity with a dual‑reviewer reference standard on a large sample of 15,307 abstracts [R0073]." — Wrong study cited. The sample size of 15,307 abstracts and the sensitivity of ~88-89% belong to Nordmann et al. (2026) [R0073], not Yamoah et al. (2026) [R0096]. Yamoah et al. studied a sample of 8,277 records and achieved 91.18% sensitivity.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the citation to [R0073] (Nordmann et al.) or correct the author name to Nordmann et al. If referring to Yamoah et al., the sample size should be 8,277 and sensitivity 91.18%.

issues.description: Unsupported statement: "Across three reviews (7,693–21,116 records), compact models using structured prompts achieved up to 100% sensitivity but low precision (<10%); balanced accuracy varied from 76.7% to 91.3% and specificity reached 92.7% for the best model [R0072]." — The evidence card for [R0072] lists only two specific record counts (21,116 for AB review and 7,693 for COVID-19 review) and states the study involved 'three systematic reviews'. It does not provide the record count for the third review, so the range '7,693–21,116' is not fully supported by the provided evidence text. Additionally, while the findings mention 'low precision below 10%', the specific value '92.7%' for specificity is listed in the 'Effects' section but not explicitly linked to 'the best model' in the narrative findings, though this is a minor interpretation. The primary issue is the unsupported range implying all three reviews fall within that specific min-max range without evidence for the third.
issues.suggested_fix: Change 'Across three reviews (7,693–21,116 records)' to 'Across three reviews (including datasets of 7,693 and 21,116 records)' or simply 'Across three reviews' to avoid asserting a range that covers all three without explicit data for the third.

issues.description: "Certainty of evidence was rated moderate to low." — The thematic synthesis explicitly rates the certainty as 'moderate' for all four themes. The abstract introduces a 'low' rating that is not supported by the provided synthesis.
issues.suggested_fix: Change 'moderate to low' to 'moderate' to align with the certainty ratings in the synthesis.

issues.description: "Fine-tuned, domain-specific LLMs demonstrated superior balanced accuracy compared with general-purpose models, achieving sensitivities around 81–91% and specificities up to 96% [R0069,R0096,R0072,R0045,R0058,R0085]." — The citation list includes R0045, R0058, and R0085, which the synthesis identifies as non-fine-tuned or general-purpose models (GPT-4 evaluation, Llama-3.1 zero-shot, GPT-4 prompt engineering). Including them in the sentence describing 'Fine-tuned' models is factually incorrect and contradicts the synthesis's distinction between fine-tuned and general-purpose performance.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove R0045, R0058, and R0085 from the citation list for the fine-tuned model claim, or restructure the sentence to separate fine-tuned results from general-purpose comparisons.
